metadata.title: Does Claude's Macro Rates Dashboard Predict Where Rates Are Headed?
metadata.purpose: Answer whether asking Claude for a macro rates monitor dashboard means it forecasts where rates are headed -- or is doing something more mechanical. Lands the carry-out that the skill combines four named inputs by a fixed procedure, and a finished dashboard means the combination ran correctly, not that reality will follow it.

beats.narration_text: Someone asks whether a macro rates dashboard means Claude is predicting where rates are headed next. It isn't. Liam is here to take you through what the skill actually combines, and what it leaves alone.

beats.narration_text: The natural guess is that asking Claude for a macro rates dashboard means it's forming its own view on where the economy is headed -- reading the data and telling you what's coming. But the skill is a fixed procedure: it combines four named things -- macro indicators, the yield curve, inflation breakevens, and swap rates -- using the relationships already defined for them, like splitting a yield into its real and nominal parts. Ask it instead to forecast what the central bank will actually do next quarter, and there's nothing to run: that's not one of the four things the spec combines.

shot.new_visual_element: An analyst forecasting, struck; a four-input combination chain, lit

production_viz.label: Forecast, struck -- four inputs combined, lit
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a card labelled 'FORECAST' with a figure guessing an arrow up or down. Right: a card labelled 'FOUR INPUTS, COMBINED' listing three grouped lines. The forecast side dims and gets a terracotta strike; the four-input side stays lit. A final line reads 'central bank's next move -- can't run' and the chain does not reach for it.

beats.narration_text: What the skill actually does: it takes macro indicators as one input, the shape of the yield curve as a second, inflation breakevens -- the market's implied inflation expectation -- as a third, and swap rates as a fourth, and combines all four into one dashboard. Watch the anchor: one pull of market data moving through all four building blocks, in order, before it reaches the dashboard. Each block uses only the definition the file gives it -- nothing added, nothing guessed.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- one data package traveling through INDICATORS -> YIELD CURVE -> BREAKEVENS -> SWAP RATES, in order, to DASHBOARD

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- one package, four inputs
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Four stacked cards labelled 'INDICATORS', 'YIELD CURVE', 'BREAKEVENS', 'SWAP RATES', plus a fifth 'DASHBOARD' card at the bottom. A single highlighted token 'MARKET DATA PULL' travels down through the four cards in turn, each lighting as it arrives, never skipping ahead of an unlit card, then arrives at DASHBOARD. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS, PAID OFF, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: The data package comes out the other side as a finished dashboard -- but that only proves the four building blocks were combined the way the file defines them: nothing skipped, nothing improvised. It doesn't prove the economic read inside the dashboard will hold up -- a correctly computed breakeven can still turn out to be a poor predictor of actual inflation. And if swap-rate data isn't available and that block can't populate, that's a data gap, not evidence the other three blocks are wrong.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS, resting at DASHBOARD; splits into 'ran is not sound' and 'missing is not wrong'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- dashboard, then split
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 FOUR-CARD COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical placement, the token resting at the 'DASHBOARD' card. It shrinks and slides up. Two cards fade in beneath: left reads 'RAN: BREAKEVEN' with a checkmark, then a struck-through 'SOUND?' beneath it, labelled 'ran is not sound'; right reads 'MISSING: SWAP RATES' beside a faint 'data gap, not wrong' note, labelled 'missing is not wrong'.

beats.narration_text: A macro rates dashboard from Claude isn't an original economic call -- it's four named inputs, macro indicators, yield curve, breakevens, and swap rates, combined by one fixed, repeatable procedure. A finished dashboard means the combination ran correctly, not that reality will follow it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt -- read it with me. Pick a country or region you follow. Ask Claude to pull together a macro rates read combining the yield curve shape, inflation breakevens, and swap rates -- and have it show you the definition it's using for each piece before it combines them. Then ask it what the central bank will actually do next quarter, and watch what it can and can't answer. Liam, in for Bear.
